questionText:
Consider a database that has the relation schema CR(StudentName, CourseName). An instance of the schema CR is as given below.

CR
StudentNameCourseName
SACA
SACB
SACC
SBCB
SBCC
SCCA
SCCB
SCCC
SDCA
SDCB
SDCC
SDCD
SECD
SECA
SECB
SFCA
SFCB
SFCC

The following query is made on the database.

$$T1 \leftarrow \pi_{\text{CourseName}}(\sigma_{\text{StudentName}='SA'}(\text{CR}))$$
$$T2 \leftarrow \text{CR} \div T1$$

The number of rows in $T2$ is ___________.
explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate relation T1
The query $T1 \leftarrow \pi_{\text{CourseName}}(\sigma_{\text{StudentName}='SA'}(\text{CR}))$ projects the course names associated with student 'SA'.
From the table, student 'SA' is enrolled in courses: $CA, CB, CC$.
Therefore, $T1 = \{CA, CB, CC\}$.

Step 2: Apply the Division Operator ($\div$)
The division $T2 \leftarrow \text{CR} \div T1$ finds all student names ($StudentName$) who are associated with ALL courses present in $T1$ (i.e., $CA, CB,$ and $CC$).

Step 3: Check each student's courses
• SA: Enrolled in $\{CA, CB, CC\}$ $\rightarrow$ Contains all required courses.
• SB: Enrolled in $\{CB, CC\}$ $\rightarrow$ Missing $CA$.
• SC: Enrolled in $\{CA, CB, CC\}$ $\rightarrow$ Contains all required courses.
• SD: Enrolled in $\{CA, CB, CC, CD\}$ $\rightarrow$ Contains all required courses.
• SE: Enrolled in $\{CD, CA, CB\}$ $\rightarrow$ Missing $CC$.
• SF: Enrolled in $\{CA, CB, CC\}$ $\rightarrow$ Contains all required courses.

Step 4: Count the matching rows
The students included in relation $T2$ are $SA, SC, SD,$ and $SF$.
Hence, the number of rows in $T2$ is 4.
